page0.text:
It smells like rain.
The courtyard is empty, devoid of churchgoers.
Instead, I come across...
A man waiting for me, without his mistress.

page1.text:
Strangely, I don't even wonder what he's doing here,
or why he was waiting for me.

page2.text:
The red knight watches me quietly for a moment, and then closes his eyes, as if coming to a decision.
"I'm sure you understand, Shirou Emiya.
What you are fighting. Whom you must kill."
He gives a clearer answer than I ever could.

page3.text:
...
The words are enough to freeze my heart cold.
...I know.
I said that I'd fight to put a stop to the war and keep innocent people from being caught up in the Masters' conflict.

page4.text:
I asked Saber for help to carry out that decision.
I won't hide from that.
And now...Sakura is the Master I need to stop before anyone else.

page5.text:
...
...I acknowledge it, but I can't say it out loud.
...
The red knight says nothing.
We both stand there under the overcast sky, watching one another.

page6.text:
"...Then do what you want. My objective has changed. Now that it has appeared, the time for personal vendettas is past."
"Huh...?"

page7.text:
"This is a warning.
If you intend to stay true to your principles, then go ahead.
But if you choose a different path, then Shirou Emiya has no future."
"You mean I'm going to die?"

page8.text:
"If you consider death the same as denying who you are.
Until now, you've lived your life for the sake of everyone. Isn't that right? How can you twist your oath into abandoning everyone else so that one person may live?"

page9.text:
His assertion doesn't carry a note of irony.
I sense some kind of determination...and emptiness...in Archer's words.

page10.text:
"I don't know or care which path Shirou Emiya will choose.
But if you are going to deny everything you are and try to protect a single person...you will be judged for that sin."

page11.text:
His footsteps fade into the distance.
I start down the hill, plagued by doubts.

page12.text:
Before I know it, I'm sitting on a park bench.
I don't feel like going home, but I can't wait at the church, either.

page13.text:
This park is far from both my house and the church.
...It's been a few hours since I learned that Sakura is a Master.
It's the perfect waiting spot to symbolize how I'm sitting on the fence, unable to make up my mind about anything.

page14.text:
...
An answer.
I need to come up with an answer, but my thoughts are scattered, and I can't figure out what I'm supposed to think about.

page15.text:
...As the Matou heir, she has been experimented on for years.
It isn't difficult to imagine what sort of education Zouken had in store for her. Sakura Matou is not the chaste maiden you wish her to be, but a witch sullied by his worms.

page16.text:
"Shut...up..."
I don't need him to repeat that to me.
Even an upstart mage like me knows that.
What it means, and everything she's had to go through. Why didn't...

page17.text: While she tried to keep the truth from you, she always sought salvation. If you could not even realise that, you have no right to have feelings for her.

page18.text:
"Shut up, shut up, shut up! I know! I don't need you to tell me that!"
Why...didn't...
I notice at all?

page19.text:
"Ngh..."
My molars are broken.
I've been clenching my jaw so much today, it would be a wonder if my teeth didn't break.

page20.text:
"Dammit. Dammit, dammit, dammit!"
I crush exposed nerves.
The pain stabs into my head.
It can't even tear apart the hatred in my mind.

page21.text:
...
A fire blazes in my brain.
When I think back on all our time together, now that I know the truth, it drives me crazy.

page22.text:
Sakura was laughing.
She always smiling peacefully.
And I just basked in it, oblivious to all of her suffering.

page23.text:
...It doesn't matter now whether her smile was genuine or forced.
Now, when I realize how much pain she was hiding behind her smile, it makes me want to kill someone.

page24.text:
"Zouken...Matou...!"
I can't forgive him.
I don't need him to atone. I just want to erase him right now from Sakura's life.

page25.text:
It's all his fault.
If not for Zouken, Sakura would have grown up like any other girl. She never would've had those bizarre Crest Worms implanted in her.
If not for Zouken, she never would have become a Master, Shinji would never have fallen so far, and they would've lived normal lives.
That's why...
If I can just get rid of him, then all this will...!

page26.text:
I punch the bench,
tearing open the wound on my left hand, and splattering the white bench with red blood.
The colorful contrast brings me to my senses.

page27.text:
"I'm so weak, saying that. What can I even do about it?"
I run out of pity for my own stupidity.

page28.text:
"...That doesn't matter. Blaming people won't fix anything."
But does it make me feel any better?
I won't deny what Zouken's done to Sakura, what he's here to do now.
Thinking about it disgusts me, and, like a snake's tongue flicking out, makes me feel envy at having something precious stolen from me.

page29.text:
It doesn't make my failures any better, either.
I'm the one who didn't notice it.
No matter what Zouken might've done, I was the only person who failed to notice any of it.

page30.text:
"No. I didn't fail to realize it. I..."
...didn't even try to notice.
The night I faced off against Zouken.
He said that Sakura wasn't involved, and I believed him.

page31.text:
...What an idiot I am.
Why did I believe what he said?
As long as Sakura's one of the Matous, there's no way she isn't related.
The night I lost Saber, I experienced firsthand how that fiend Zouken views human life.
He gave Rider to Shinji, so he'd be just as willing to do something to Sakura.

page32.text:
And yet...
I ate up every lie he fed me, just because it would've been convenient if they were true.

page33.text:
I actually did notice, back then.
I would've arrived at the truth, if I'd just thought about it a little.
...That's why I wasn't surprised.
When I learned Sakura was a Master and that she'd endured an upbringing that she could never talk about, it all felt obvious to me.
I tried not to think about it because I couldn't bear to come to terms with it.

page34.text:
If I noticed it, then I'd have to fight.
If Zouken Matou is evil to other humans,
then the right thing to do would be to fight the evildoer.

page35.text:
...
No...
The right path is already laid out for me.
If Sakura becomes Zouken's puppet and makes Rider indiscriminately attack people again, then there's only one thing for me to do.

page36.text:
That's why I've trained myself in magecraft and lived the way I do:
to save people from disasters beyond their control.

page37.text:
"Ngh..."
So, I already know what to do.
The red knight was right.

page38.text: Senpai, if I become a bad person...

page39.text:
I don't want to hurt Sakura, and I sympathize with her.
But she isn't an exception.
No matter how precious she is to me, if it means allowing another tragedy to happen...

page40.text: As long as it's you, Senpai.

page41.text:
"Urgh, brrgh...!"
...then I have to eliminate her.
It's nothing to hesitate about. So why...?
"Hah... uugh... guh...!"
Why am I trying so hard to keep down the vomit rising to my throat...?

page42.text:
"Ah... hah, hah, hah..."
I endure the nausea.
...I wonder how long I've been sitting here.
I don't have time to fixate on trivial thoughts.
Tohsaka said she'd be back once the surgery is finished.
The town smells like rain.
I'll go back to the church and check on Sakura one more time before it starts to pour. Then—

page43.text:
"Let's play, Shirou!"
Something crashes into me.
I'm suddenly hugged from behind.

page44.text:
"...Illya."
Even without turning around, I know who it is.
This pale girl is the person I always meet in this park.

page45.text:
"Ehehe! Did I scare you? I saw you walking around town, so I came to see you!"
Illya laughs cheerfully.

page46.text:
...
Her innocence hurts.
I know it's selfish, but right now, I don't want to see anyone laughing.

page47.text:
"Ah. Why are you ignoring me, Shirou? It's rude to sulk when a girl is talking to you."
"..."
...I wish she'd be quiet.
To be honest, I don't have time for this right now.

page48.text:
"Mrgh! Hey, Shirou! You should listen when people are speaking to you!"
"...Illya. Sorry, but I don't have time for this.
Go play by yourself."

page49.text:
"Aww, but that's boring. I came all the way here to see you.
You haven't come by since then, and if I let you go today, you won't show up again."

page50.text: "...We never promised to meet here every day. Plus, it's nighttime. Aren't Masters supposed to kill each other if they see each other at night?"

page51.text:
As soon as I say those unkind words, my nausea returns.
...I despise myself so much I want to hit myself.
Illya's just trying to make me feel better, but I'm pushing her away.

page52.text:
"Why? You're not a Master anymore, so I can just let you leave."
"...! You know I'm not a Master anymore, Illya?"

page53.text:
"Mm-hm! I know everything! You lost Saber, and Rin lost to Rider. But Rider's Master collapsed, so there are only two of us left, right?"
Illya recounts it all cheerfully.

page54.text:
...
It almost sounds like she's laughing at Sakura's fate.

page55.text:
"Victory is within sight. Rider's Master is going to self-destruct, and Archer's no big deal.
Now that Saber's gone, there's no one left who can beat my Berserker.
So come on, let's play! You're not a Master anymore, so I'll invite you to my castle!"

page56.text:
Illya rudely tries to hug me.
Her carefree smile irritates me.
"Shut up! I told you I don't have time! Go play by yourself!"
"Aah!?"
I shove Illya away in anger.

page57.text:
"Ah..."
It's too late to regret it.
Illya stands there in surprise.
I don't have to look at her to tell how shocked she is.

page58.text:
...I threw aside her sincere goodwill.
All of the kindness she's shown me just went down the drain.

page60.text:
"..."
I bow, unable to bear the silence.
"Sorry, Shirou."
A small hand strokes my hair.

page62.text:
"Illya...aren't you mad?"
"I'm not mad. You look like you're about to cry, you know. I don't know what happened, but I'd feel sorry for you if I hated you too. So no matter what you do, I'll be on your side."

page63.text:
...
Pure white fills my vision.
...That one sentence.
Those simple words wash all the turmoil from my mind.

page64.text:
"On... my side...?"
"Yeah. It's only natural to protect someone you love, right?
Even I know that."

page65.text:
She'll be on my side.
Just like that, Illya says her reason for being someone's ally.
